title: Aston Martin Unveils Vanquish 25: A 50-Unit Tribute to 25 Years of Its V12 Grand Tourer
excerpt: Limited to 25 coupes and 25 Volantes, the Vanquish 25 celebrates the nameplate's quarter-century with bespoke Q finishes and starts at $596,300.
body:
• Aston Martin has revealed the Vanquish 25, a strictly limited run of 50 cars — 25 coupes and 25 Volantes — marking the nameplate's 25th anniversary.
  • Created by Q by Aston Martin, each car wears an exclusive Skye Silver finish with metal foil detailing and heritage-inspired interior touches.
  • US pricing starts at $596,300 for the coupe and $634,700 for the Volante, with first deliveries in Q4 2026.
  • The car retains the current Vanquish's 824 hp twin-turbo V12, capable of 214 mph and 0-62 mph in 3.3 seconds.

Aston Martin has pulled the covers off the Vanquish 25, a commemorative limited edition that marks a quarter-century since the original V12 Vanquish first appeared in 2001. Production is capped at a total of 50 units worldwide — split evenly between 25 coupes and 25 Volantes — each created by the British marque's bespoke Q commissioning division.

The anniversary model will make its public debut at Monterey Car Week, running August 10–16, with first customer deliveries scheduled for the fourth quarter of 2026. Units will be allocated globally on a first-come, first-served basis, according to an Aston Martin spokesperson.

Heritage Through Restraint

Rather than engineering a stripped-down track weapon, Aston Martin opted for a masterclass in understated elegance. The exterior is defined by an exclusive Q Skye Silver paint finish — a colour unavailable on any other model — complemented by metal foil detailing on the side sills and shield vanes that adds visual depth without overwrought contrast.

Unique stainless steel side strakes, a custom Q Commission exhaust finisher, and a set of 21-inch forged alloy wheels featuring a diamond-turned "V" motif round out the exterior distinctions.

"Vanquish 25 builds on the extraordinary achievements of the modern, third-generation Vanquish with a carefully curated package that subtly celebrates this important milestone in our history."

— Vittorio Gabba, Head of Q at Aston Martin

Interior Nods to the 2001 Original

Inside, the anniversary theme is expressed through laser-etched trim inlays and "Vanquish 25" embroidery on the seatbacks. A red centre-accented start-stop rotary button pays homage to a design detail from the original Ian Callum-penned car — a nod that Aston Martin aficionados will recognise immediately.

The Engine That Defines It

Mechanically, the Vanquish 25 remains identical to the current third-generation model. It is powered by a twin-turbocharged 5.2-litre V12 producing 824 horsepower and 738 lb-ft of torque, paired exclusively with a ZF eight-speed automatic transmission driving the rear wheels.

In its most aggressive setting, the Vanquish 25 can reach 62 mph from standstill in 3.3 seconds and hit a top speed of 214 mph. It remains one of the fastest grand tourers on sale — and potentially one of the last V12-powered Aston Martins, with reports suggesting the engine can only survive through the end of the decade under tightening emissions regulations.

Pricing and Legacy

In the United States, the Vanquish 25 starts at $596,300 for the coupe and $634,700 for the Volante. International pricing has not been disclosed.

The original Vanquish debuted in 2001 as Aston Martin's most technically advanced car of its era, and earned pop-culture immortality when James Bond drove an invisible version in Die Another Day. Three generations later, the nameplate remains central to the brand's identity as a builder of V12 grand tourers — a tradition the Vanquish 25 is designed to honour while it still can.
